title: Claims Manual: One Occurrence Damaging Several Covered Vehicles
content:
Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), one occurrence sometimes damages two or more vehicles covered for the same named insured. Examples are a hailstorm, a flood, or a collision between two of the household's own vehicles. Such losses are handled vehicle by vehicle.

**Clause.**
- Each damaged vehicle of one occurrence is its own claim, with its own claim number and its own deductible under its own package.
- Deductibles are never combined or waived because several vehicles were damaged.
- A collision between two of the named insured's own vehicles is a collision loss on each of them.

The claim and the deductible follow each vehicle's own coverage record, as the system shows it.

### Hypothetical illustration

A hailstorm damages two vehicles of one named insured. One is covered on the Cardinal Point Physical Damage $1,000 Deductible package and the other on the Cardinal Point Physical Damage $500 Deductible package. The result is two claims with two claim numbers. Each claim carries the comprehensive deductible of its own vehicle's package. Neither deductible is combined with the other or waived.

| Occurrence | Claims opened | Deductibles |
|---|---|---|
| Hail damages two covered vehicles | Two, one per vehicle | One per claim, each under its own package |
| Two household vehicles collide with each other | Two, one per vehicle | The collision deductible of each vehicle's package |
